faq: What size hay barn do I need?

It depends on your bale type, how high you stack, and the room you need for your loader. Large round bales, large square bales, and small square bales each need different space. Tell us your bale size and how much hay you store, and we will size the building to fit.
Can a hay barn be open on the sides?
Yes. A hay barn can have an open front, partial sidewalls, or full sidewalls. The right layout depends on your site, weather exposure, and how you load and unload.
Can I store feed against the wall?
Yes, with the right design. A stemwall, commonly around 4 feet high, lets you store feed against the wall line. Tell us what you will store so the wall is designed for it.
Are your buildings designed for heavy snow?
Your building is engineered for the snow loads required at your site, including the heavy loads common in mountain valleys like Star Valley. Requirements are set by your local building department.
Can I replace an old pole barn with a steel building?
Yes. Many owners replace or upgrade older pole barns with steel buildings engineered for their site. Tell us the size and use and we will plan the replacement.
Many ranchers and farmers assemble their own buildings. Your building package arrives with the parts and components cut and sized for assembly, or you can hire a contractor.
Can I add on or add lean-tos later?
Yes. Steel buildings can often be designed so bays or lean-tos can be added later. Let us know your plans so the design allows for it.
How long does it take to get an agricultural steel building?
Our current turnaround is 8 to 10 weeks. Timelines can vary with project size, options, and demand.
